exceptions.rationale: Affects only filelock's SQLite-backed ReadWriteLock/AsyncReadWriteLock, exploitable by a local user who can write to the lock directory. Nothing in the backend uses them: huggingface-hub takes FileLock/SoftFileLock and litellm FileLock in its proxy CLI. The fix (4.2.1) is blocked because every current litellm (1.104-1.107 pre-releases) requires filelock<4.0; bump once litellm allows 4.x.

Windows-only denial of service on the SQLite-backed ReadWriteLock/AsyncReadWriteLock by a local account; the backend runs on Linux and uses neither class. Fix (4.2.1) blocked by litellm's filelock<4.0 requirement, as for CVE-2026-112940.

Windows-only: a local account holding an oplock on a soft-lock marker stalls acquire(). The backend runs on Linux, where FileLock uses fcntl and the soft-lock oplock path does not exist. Fix (4.2.1) blocked by litellm's filelock<4.0 requirement, as for CVE-2026-112940.
